facts.text: Holiday City-Berkeley sits just 43 feet above sea level, making it especially susceptible to coastal flooding and tidal influences.
Before Europeans arrived, the area that is now Holiday City-Berkeley was part of the Lenni Lenape Unalachtigo territory, the “People who live near the ocean.”.
Cedar Creek ran through the community, providing a vital oyster source and supporting seasonal campsites for the nomadic Lenni Lenape bands.
In the 19th century, sawmills in Holiday City-Berkeley processed cedar into shingles, turning once-swampy land into productive agricultural fields.
The community is a retirement enclave; only residents over 55 can own property or join its recreational activities.
Holiday City-Berkeley's wetlands are shaped by its proximity to Barnegat Bay, creating diverse aquatic habitats and influencing local water flow.
